_about: Curated, dated quantities for the hypothetical 'What backs a dollar?' calculator. Every entry links to its official source. Prices are NOT stored here: they come from data/latest.json (spot_last_known) or are fetched from FRED by scripts/compute_resource_backing.py. Edit a quantity only when its source publishes a new figure, and update as_of + source_url with it.

troy_oz_per_metric_ton_source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Silver (footnote: 1 metric ton = 32,150.7 troy oz)

mmbtu_per_mcf_source.name: EIA: Energy units and calculators explained (1 cubic foot = 1,036 Btu)

coal.label: Average US coal sales price, all ranks (2024 annual)

items.name: US Treasury silver (US Mint stocks)
items.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Silver (Stocks, Treasury; source: US Mint, working and deep-storage stocks)
items.note: Working stock for coin programs, not a monetary reserve. The US holds no official silver reserve.

items.name: US silver reserves in the ground
items.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Silver (World Mine Production and Reserves)
items.note: Unmined, mostly owned by mining companies or private/state mineral owners. Valued at spot before any mining cost.

items.name: COMEX vault silver (registered + eligible)
items.source_name: CME warehouse reports via The Vault Report
items.note: Privately owned metal stored in US vaults (some by foreign owners). Off by default.

items.name: US official gold reserve
items.source_name: US Treasury: Status Report of U.S. Government Gold Reserve
items.note: Official statutory value is $42.22/oz; valued here at market spot.

items.name: US gold reserves in the ground
items.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Gold (World Mine Production and Reserves)
items.note: Unmined, mostly privately held mining claims. Valued at spot before any mining cost.

items.name: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude
items.source_name: US DOE: SPR Quick Facts (inventory by site)
items.note: Owned by the US Department of Energy. Not part of EIA proved reserves.

items.name: US proved crude oil + lease condensate reserves
items.source_name: EIA: U.S. Crude Oil and Natural Gas Proved Reserves, Year-End 2024 (Table 1)
items.note: In the ground; mostly privately or state owned, some under federal leases. Valued at spot before any production cost.

items.name: US proved natural gas reserves (dry gas content)
items.source_name: EIA: Proved Reserves Year-End 2024 (Table 11, dry natural gas content of 583,942 Bcf wet gas)
items.note: Natural gas plant liquids (34,072 million barrels) are not valued. Converted at 1.036 MMBtu per thousand cubic feet.

items.name: US recoverable coal reserves at producing mines
items.note: EIA's broader 'estimated recoverable reserves' (249,351 million short tons) is not used because most of it is not economic to mine at today's prices.

items.name: US copper reserves in the ground
items.source_name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Copper (World Mine Production and Reserves)
items.note: Unmined. Valued at the global price before any mining cost.

items.name: Federal land, lower 48 states
items.source_name: BEA working paper WP2015-3, Larson, 'New Estimates of Value of Land of the United States'
items.note: 2009 dollars, not updated. Excludes Alaska and Hawaii (where most federal acreage is). Context: about 615.2M acres are managed by five federal agencies, ~640M acres total (CRS R42346, Sept 30, 2024).

items.name: Non-federal land, lower 48 states
items.source_name: BEA working paper WP2015-3 (total $23.0T minus $1.8T federal)
items.note: 2009 dollars, not updated. Mostly private, state, local and tribal land. Larson's land values include timber and water rights that convey with the land.

context.source_name: CRS R42346, Federal Land Ownership: Overview and Data (updated Sept 14, 2026)
context.federal_mineral_estate_note: BLM also administers 700M+ acres of federal subsurface mineral estate, so part of the oil, gas and coal reserves is federally owned, but EIA does not split its totals by owner.

left_out.name: Timber
left_out.reason: No credible current national dollar valuation found. Larson (BEA) land values already include timber that conveys with the land, so adding it would double count.

left_out.name: Natural gas plant liquids
left_out.reason: EIA reports 34,072 million barrels in proved reserves, but there is no single public NGL price series to value them on, so they are not counted.

left_out.name: Critical minerals other than copper (lithium, rare earths, etc.)
left_out.reason: USGS reserve figures exist for some, but there is no reliable public spot price for most, so they are left out rather than guessed.

left_out.name: Federal buildings, roads and other property
left_out.reason: Not natural resources; outside this comparison.
